$note: Does a source REGISTER publish an application window, independently of whether
a value came back for any given row? A property of the register, not of our
copy -- inferring it from windows PRESENT in the copy is what made the earlier
safeguard self-cancelling: a copy stale enough to be dangerous has none, so it
withheld nothing on exactly the corpus it existed to protect.
RECONSTRUCTED 2026-08-09 from funding_instruments.source_window_policy in
Railway Postgres. The original was written by a workstream, never force-added
past the `data` gitignore, and lost with its worktree -- it exists in no branch
and no commit. assign_source_window_policy.py failed on every machine while the
definition survived only as values in one database. That is the orphan shape
this repo keeps finding, in its purest form.
Keyed family -> country, because one family can publish windows in one register
and not another. Where a family/country carried both values the majority won,
and every such split is recorded below rather than smoothed away.
SHAPE REPAIRED 2026-08-09 (wsBX). The reconstruction above recovered the
VALUES but wrote them as policies[family][country], a shape
assign_source_window_policy.py cannot read: it contracts for a
`declarations` list matched on id / id_prefix / root_id /
source_family_bucket. So the script raised KeyError('declarations') on every
machine from the day of the reconstruction, no row loaded after it was ever
asked about its register, and check_liveness went red on 41 Spanish BDNS
convocatorias -- correctly, since NULL means nobody asked.
COUNTRY IS A MATCH KEY, and that is why the two shapes could not be
reconciled by rewriting this file alone. A family does NOT have one answer:
state_aid_satr publishes application windows in ES (175 rows) and in none of
the other twenty countries it covers, and national_dev_banks publishes them
in FR and nowhere else. Folding country away would have had to smooth one of
those into the other -- losing a true distinction to make a script run. The
script's MATCH_KEYS gained `country` instead, ranked narrower than
source_family_bucket so a family/country declaration beats a family-wide one.
WINDOWS LOADED 2026-08-09 (wsCO2), on the owner's approval of workstream
CO's finding. Every per-id declaration below carries `closed_on`, which is
a date the REGISTER states for that object, quoted in `closed_note`. None
is a heuristic and none is an inference: a row whose register answers with
no date at all is left with no declaration and stays unknown, because
'we do not know' is a legitimate state and asserting either openness or
closure without evidence is the defect.
The 39 TEE rows whose data.gouv.fr CSV row has an empty `date_cloture`
were NOT read as open-ended. That column is the thin index liveness.ts
already documents -- empty for 93 of the 107 dispositifs whose pages state
a closing date -- so its silence is our copy's, one level up. They were
asked of the per-slug TEE endpoint and the dispositif page instead.
